sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Jainism** is an ancient Śramaṇa religion of India that prescribes a path of non-violence (**Ahimsa**) towards all living beings.
Originated in the **6th Century BCE**, contemporary with Buddhism and the second urbanization period of ancient India.
Origin and early spread occurred in the Gangetic plains, primarily in **Bihar**, **Uttar Pradesh**, and **Magadha**.
Founded by **Rishabhanatha** (1st Tirthankara), structurally organized by **Parshvanatha** (23rd), and historically established by **Mahavira** (24th Tirthankara).
Crucial for UPSSSC PET due to questions on **Tirthankaras**, **Mahavira's birth/death**, Jain councils, and philosophical concepts like **Triratna** and **Anekantavada**.
Extreme asceticism, rejection of **Vedic authority**, denial of a supreme creator God, and emphasis on strict **penance** and karma.
High-yielding static GK topic appearing frequently in general awareness and ancient Indian history sections.
**Agamas** (canonical texts of Svetambara Jainism) and **Purvas** (lost ancient texts).
Split into **Digambara** (sky-clad, naked monks) and **Svetambara** (white-robed monks) around the 3rd century BCE.

items.title: 1. Life and Journey of Lord Mahavira
items.content:
• Original Name: **Vardhamana**
• Birthplace: **Kundagrama** near **Vaishali**, Bihar
• Birth Year: **540 BCE** (traditional) or **599 BCE**
• Family: Father **Siddharth** (head of Jnatrika Kshatriya clan), Mother **Trishala** (sister of Lichchhavi king Chetaka)
• Wife: **Yasoda**; Daughter: **Priyadarsana** (Anojja)
• Renunciation: Left home at age **30** after parents' death with permission of brother **Nandivardhana**
• Enlightenment (Kevala Jnana): Gained under a **Sal tree** at **Jrimbhikagrama** on the bank of river **Rijupalika** at age **42**
• Nirvana (Death): **468 BCE** at age **72** in **Pava** (near modern Rajgir, Bihar) in the palace of king **Sipati/Hastipal**

items.title: 2. The Five Great Vows (Mahavratas)
items.content:
• **Ahimsa**: Non-injury/Non-violence in thought, word, and deed
• **Satya**: Speaking the truth
• **Asteya**: Non-stealing (not taking what is not given)
• **Brahmacharya**: Celibacy/Chastity (added by **Mahavira**)
• **Aparigraha**: Non-possession/Non-attachment to worldly goods
• *Note: First 4 were given by **Parshvanatha**; 5th was added by **Mahavira**.*
• **Mnemonic for Vows:** **"A Smart Aunt Buys Apples"** -> **A**himsa, **S**atya, **A**steya, **B**rahmacharya, **A**parigraha.

items.title: 3. Three Jewels of Jainism (Triratna)
items.content:
• **Samyak Darshana** (Right Faith): Believing in the teachings of Jinas and Tirthankaras
• **Samyak Jnana** (Right Knowledge): Comprehending the true nature of the universe
• **Samyak Charitra** (Right Conduct): Practicing the five vows and leading a disciplined moral life
• **Mnemonic for Triratna:** **"DKC"** (Like a Doctor's degree) -> **D**arshana (Faith), **K**nana (Knowledge), **C**haritra (Conduct).

items.title: 4. Jain Councils and Literature
items.content:
• **First Jain Council:** Held at **Pataliputra** in **300 BCE**; chaired by **Sthulabahu**; resulted in the compilation of **12 Angas**.
• **Second Jain Council:** Held at **Vallabhi** (Gujarat) in **512 CE**; chaired by **Devardhi Kshamasramana**; finalized the final version of the **12 Upangas** and **Agamas**.
• **Language of Texts:** Early texts written in **Prakrit** (Ardhamagadhi), later commentaries in **Sanskrit** and **Apabhramsha**.

items.title: 5. Core Philosophical Concepts
items.content:
• **Anekantavada**: Theory of plurality of views (many-sided reality)
• **Syadavada**: Theory of conditional predication ("maybe so")
• **Jiva**: Living soul/consciousness
• **Ajiva**: Non-living matter
• **Karma**: Binding of particles of sin and virtue to the soul; liberation (**Moksha**) requires shedding all karma through severe asceticism.

sections.title: Comprehensive Data Tables
rows: Associated with Lord Krishna in Puranic legends; symbol is **Conch**.
Historical figure; prince of Varanasi; gave **4 vows**; symbol is **Snake**.
Last Tirthankara; real organizer of Jainism; symbol is **Lion**.
Adopted daughter of Dadhivahana of Champa.
**Bhadrabahu** led the southern migration to Karnataka during famine; his followers became **Digambara**.
Remained in Magadha during the 12-year famine; his followers wore white robes and became **Svetambara**.
Mahavira's chief disciple (Ganadhara) who outlived him.
King of Magadha who shifted capital to Pataliputra and patronized Jainism.
King of Kalinga; carved Hathigumpha inscription; built caves for Jaina monks in **Udayagiri-Khandagiri**.
Abdicated throne, became a Jain monk under Bhadrabahu, and died by **Sallehkhana** at **Shravanabelagola**.

items.definition: Use the acronym **"R A A S A"** -> **R**ishabhanatha (1st), **A**jitnatha (2nd), **S**ambhavanatha (3rd), **Abhinandananatha** (4th), **Sumatinatha** (5th).
Remember numbers **30-12-72** -> Left home at age **30**, attained enlightenment after **12** years of penance (at age 42), and attained Nirvana at age **72**.
Association trick: **Digambara** sounds like direction (**Disa** / sky) -> Sky-clad (naked). **Svetambara** -> **Sweta** means white -> White-robed.
Acronym **"PV"** (Primary Version) -> **P**ataliputra (1st Council) and **V**allabhi (2nd Council).
Rishabhanatha = **Bull** (strong like a bull at start), Parshvanatha = **Snake** (hooded protection), Mahavira = **Lion** (king of beasts, final Tirthankara).

items.term: Trick 6: River and Tree of Enlightenment
items.definition: Think of **R**ijupalika river and **S**al tree -> **R & S** (like a Report Card score for enlightenment).
Students often confuse **Rishabhanatha** (founder of the religion/tradition) with **Mahavira** (the 24th and real historical organizer who consolidated Jain teachings).
**Parshvanatha** is the 23rd Tirthankara (associated with snake symbol and 4 vows), while **Mahavira** is the 24th Tirthankara (added celibacy).
First Council at Pataliputra was led by **Sthulabahu** (not Bhadrabahu). Bhadrabahu went to Karnataka.
Mahavira was born in **Kundagrama** (Vaishali), NOT in Kundalavana (Kashmir, which is famous for the 4th Buddhist Council).

items.term: Mistake 5: Language of Jain vs Buddhist Texts
items.definition: Jain canonical texts were written in **Prakrit/Ardhamagadhi**, whereas early Buddhist texts were written in **Pali**.
Sallekhana is **ritual fasting to death** permitted in Jainism, not a type of temple architecture.
There are **24 Tirthankaras** (prophets/teachers) in Jainism, starting with Rishabhanatha and ending with Mahavira.
Born in **540 BCE** at Kundagrama and died in **468 BCE** at Pava.
Rejects the authority of Vedas, denies the existence of a creator God, and emphasizes supreme **Ahimsa** (non-violence).
Samyak Darshana (Faith), Samyak Jnana (Knowledge), and Samyak Charitra (Conduct).
Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya, Brahmacharya, and Aparigraha.
Jain theory of the multiplicity of truth and reality.
Epistemological theory of conditional assertion ("in some ways, it is").
Divided into **Digambara** (naked) and **Svetambara** (white-clad) due to the 12-year famine in Magadha.
Held in **300 BCE** at Pataliputra under **Sthulabahu**.
Held in **512 CE** at Vallabhi under **Devardhi Kshamasramana**.
Patronized by kings like **Chandragupta Maurya**, **Kharavela**, and the rulers of the Haryanka and Nanda dynasties.
Famous Jain monuments include **Dilwara Temples** (Mount Abu), **Shravanabelagola** (Bahubali statue), and **Udayagiri Caves**.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, always memorize the exact symbols of the 1st (Bull), 23rd (Snake), and 24th (Lion) Tirthankaras as questions frequently match symbols with names.
Focus on the differences between Svetambara and Digambara regarding clothing, salvation for women, and whether Tirthankaras take food after enlightenment.
UPSSSC often sets traps by interchanging the birthplaces and parents of Gautama Buddha and Lord Mahavira. Double-check clan names: Mahavira was Jnatrika Kshatriya; Buddha was Sakya Kshatriya.

Do not assume Jainism accepts the caste system. While it did not aggressively attack caste like early Buddhism, it taught that karma determines birth, and anyone can achieve liberation through asceticism.

keyTakeaways: Lord Mahavira was the 24th and last Tirthankara of Jainism, born at Kundagrama in 540 BCE.
Jainism rests on the Triratna (Right Faith, Right Knowledge, Right Conduct) and Five Mahavratas.
The fifth vow of Brahmacharya was added to the earlier four vows by Lord Mahavira.
The Jain community split into Digambara and Svetambara sects during the leadership of Sthulabahu and Bhadrabahu.
Jain philosophy features unique doctrines like Anekantavada, Syadavada, and Sallekhana (ritual fasting).
Important historical patrons include Chandragupta Maurya and King Kharavela of Kalinga.
Canonical scriptures are compiled in Prakrit/Ardhamagadhi known as the Agamas.
